QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_31

question.text: The CTR of a Category III AIF (which mirrors several obligations applicable to Cat I and II) requires disclosure that fund-raising has been conducted only by what mode?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12 (Table 12.1, CTR item 'Fund raising'): 'An AIF can raise funds only by way of a private placement mechanism.' This applies to all AIF categories. Public advertisements, canvassing, and exchange book-building are impermissible. The Trap: All three wrong options mirror mutual fund or public-issue practices. AIFs are private-placement-only by design. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A, XIX-B all test this rule. XXI-B PMS also permits only private placement with minimum INR 50 lakh ticket size (different minimum). Manager's Pro-Tip: Keep a compliance log of EVERY LP approach — emails, term sheets, pitch meetings — to evidence that you engaged only pre-identified accredited / sophisticated investors. Mass-email of teasers to unvetted lists can be construed as public solicitation.
